reading.body:
Madeleine Dean's AI record is legislative and symbolic, not infrastructural: no vote, bill, or contribution in this data touches data centers, power supply, or grid capacity.

The 15 events split into three kinds. There are bills she sponsored or cosponsored, including the TRAIN Act on AI transparency, the RESTRICT Act on chip export restrictions, the Preventing Deepfakes of Intimate Images Act, the TAKE IT DOWN Act, a resolution on antisemitic content on AI platforms, and two energy-adjacent measures, the Power for the People Act of 2026 and the Reverse Big Ugly Tax Breaks for Data Centers Act. There are recorded votes, all Yea, on four bills. And there are four $1,000 contributions, two from Microsoft's PAC and two from Google's NetPAC, between April 2025 and May 2026.

The two energy items are the only ones that touch the compute stack this site tracks. The Reverse Big Ugly Tax Breaks for Data Centers Act, cosponsored in September 2026, is the most recent event in the set and the only one aimed directly at data center economics. The Power for the People Act of 2026, cosponsored in April 2026, sits on the supply side. Everything else is AI governance in the narrow sense: transparency, export controls, deepfakes, platform content.

What the data does not show is causation, and the page says so. Contributions and votes are listed in date order, not linked. The contributions are small and come from corporate PACs rather than the companies themselves. The record covers one member of Congress over roughly twenty months, so it cannot describe a chamber, a party, or a trend. It also cannot say whether any bill became law, only the latest status date.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Madeleine Dean: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 16 events.
